trust_decision.summary: Which dotted class name taken from a serialized file may be imported and instantiated; at the pinned commit import_cls imports any module and returns any attribute with no prefix or base-class check, and every caller passes file-controlled strings.

landing_point.why: The summary says a crafted serialized file makes the deserializer import arbitrary classes; from_dict falls back to import_cls on the unregistered '__serializer__' string, which is the obvious generic dispatch.

fix_sites.entry_point: import_cls helper itself (used by built-in serializers and by user custom serializers, as in examples/09_serialization/00_serialization.ipynb)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/python/laboneq/serializers/implementations/workflow_options.py:63-69 and :105-107 (also qpu.py:90/114/136, quantum_element.py:44/233-234): per-type serializers composed under from_dict that read their own class-name fields ('class__', 'quantum_operations_class', 'parameter_class') from the payload, separate from the '__serializer__' dispatch

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Once from_dict only accepts registered or laboneq.* serializers, the per-type serializers look already gated ('only reached via a trusted, registered serializer'), and the class fields are meant to name user subclasses in arbitrary packages, so restricting them looks like breaking a feature; workflow options also look like a neighbouring feature.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Loading a QPU / QuantumElement / QuantumParameters / WorkflowOptions / TaskOptions whose class is a user subclass in any package (e.g. laboneq_applications.*, which does not start with 'laboneq.') must keep working, as must from_dict on a laboneq.* serializer that is not in the registry. A blanket 'laboneq.' prefix allow-list or a registry-only lookup breaks those; the published fix uses base_cls subclass checks with prefix_restrictions=None at these sites.
